chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In

the man who fasts the day of doubt from Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must make it up, even if it is so.' This is not contradictory to the first report because what is meant by this report is one who fasted the day of doubt and did not intend that it is from Sha'ban - rather he intended that it is from the month of Ramadan. For when the matter is as we mentioned, he has fasted what is not permissible for him to fast, and at that time it becomes obligatory upon him to make it up. And it indicates that when he intended that it is from Sha'ban, it is not obligatory upon him to make it up. Added to what we have mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the Day of Doubt if one intends it is Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of fasting on the 'Day of Doubt' (30th of Sha'ban) by distinguishing between the intention of the fast and the actual month. It establishes that fasting with the specific intention of Ramadan renders the fast valid but requires make-up (Qada) if it is later confirmed to be Sha'ban, as the obligation was not yet incumbent; conversely, intending it as a voluntary Sha'ban fast avoids this requirement. This ruling harmonizes with other hadiths by emphasizing that the validity depends on the worshipper's conscious intent (niyyah) regarding the month's identity.
